segments.text: Welcome to the Last Line of Defense. I'm Seth Jones, your host and president of the Defense and Security Department at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. And I am joined today by Bonnie Glaser. Bonnie is director of the China Power

Project and a senior advisor at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Bonnie, welcome to the podcast. Thank you, Seth. Really appreciate the invite. All right, we've been focusing quite a bit on the Iran war and elements of it, but

what I'd like to do today is to to get your assessment as a China expert on what the the view is from Beijing. So, just to sort of start off with the big looming question, what is your assessment of what lessons the the Chinese leadership, including Xi

Jinping, might be learning from the US-Israeli war with Iran? That that's an excellent question and actually a really difficult question because as we observed in China's lessons learned from the war in Ukraine, what China takes away is a constant

moving moving target. And typically, China is a bit more optimistic when it's a war involving another country at the beginning, which we saw in Ukraine. And then what we saw in Ukraine was about eight eight or so months afterwards, then they started to

see the negative implications and their assessments became a bit more negative. But so far, almost immediately after the US-Israeli action in in late February, early March, we saw the PLA a social media account from the PLA

actually tweet out about five official lessons, well, semi-official lessons that the PLA took. So, I'll walk you through those and then I'll also share with you what I'm hearing in terms of debates within China on how to interpret the overall lessons.

So, one of the major lessons the PLA took was the deadliest threat, the enemy within. In other words, there was lots of coverage within China about how the United States used intelligence and traitors within both Iran and Venezuela

to take down the government there. So, one thing for China is trying to understand are there any such threats within China? A second major lesson is the costliest miscalculation is blind faith in peace. So, many Chinese commentators have noted

that it's really important during peacetime to be vigilant about the prospect of war erupting. And in particular, they noted that Iran put blind faith in US negotiations and diplomacy and the United States was using our diplomacy as a guise for

preparation for military campaigns. So again, a pretty negative assessment of what's happening there. Another major lesson >> I was going to say pretty cynical that that the assessment was that the US from a Chinese perspective was never

serious about war, but was using negotiations to prepare for it. Yeah. Well, right. Right. The US was never serious about negotiations. Exactly right. Another major lesson that we saw come out was what they said called cruelest reality, the logic of superior

firepower. And that is regardless of what might be happening on the diplomatic side, economic side, what's most important is a necessarily hard military power to protect the country. And here I think China maybe taking a number of interesting lessons learned

watching the political importance that artificial intelligence has played and the US and Israeli targeting. How much demonstrated US military power. Some Chinese commentators have noted that maybe it's possible the United States is
